decisions.reason: As a newly launched sensor module with clear platform fit, its market value is still uncertain and the option value of keeping it likely exceeds its near-term carrying cost.
Because it explicitly replaces an older voltage measurement module, it looks like a core generational update in an established line and is therefore unlikely to be withdrawn quickly.
The MQTT software proxy broadens connectivity at low maintenance cost, so real-options logic strongly favors keeping it while adoption uncertainty resolves.
A CAN bus interface matches the firm's automation and embedded customer base well, and after only a short time on the market there is too little negative evidence to justify exit.
The carbon dioxide sensor module extends the sensing portfolio in a plausible application area, so management would likely preserve the option until demand becomes clearer.
The touch panel accessory is more peripheral and likely narrower in demand than core modules, but it still supports the ecosystem and has not yet clearly failed.
